pathophysiology.summary: Appendiceal obstruction and inflammation may progress to ischemia, perforation, abscess, or peritonitis.

clinicalManagement.title: Assess and stabilize
actions: Assess observations, hydration, pain, abdominal findings, and peritonitis/sepsis.
Keep fasting when surgery may be needed.
Provide analgesia, antiemetic treatment, and fluids as clinically indicated.
Escalate immediately to emergency and surgical senior review.
Initiate resuscitation and urgent source-control planning.
Use serial examination and appropriate laboratory or imaging assessment.
Consult surgery if symptoms persist or worsen.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm diagnosis and arrange definitive care
actions: Consult general surgery for suspected appendicitis or complication.
Select imaging and antimicrobial management per patient factors and local pathway.
Document diagnosis, severity, pregnancy status when relevant, and disposition.
Arrange surgical admission and definitive management planning.
Use antimicrobials when indicated by severity and local protocol.
Assess alternative diagnoses and discharge safety.
Give return precautions for worsening pain, fever, vomiting, or weakness.

Review warning symptoms requiring immediate return.
